topic: Phase 1 permits only the specification-mandated writer-local batching queue
canonical_claim: Phase 1 permits only the specification-mandated writer-local batching queue, whole-table cache, and body reuse within one fold batch as optimizations.

topic: Deleting a never-born namespace's _ckpt from a CORRUPTED_DATA conflict
canonical_claim: Deleting a never-born namespace's `_ckpt` from a `CORRUPTED_DATA` conflict path is unsafe because the conflict proves another object occupies the key, so the delete could remove a live successor's recovery checkpoint; a backstop must independently verify emptiness with a real LIST.

topic: The _registry namespace registry was removed because repeated create/drop
canonical_claim: The `_registry` namespace registry was removed because repeated create/drop operations caused monotone growth; per-shard incarnation enables namespace-level reclaim instead.

topic: Reducing admits() call frequency (backlog fix #2) was rejected
canonical_claim: Reducing admits() call frequency (backlog fix #2) was rejected as an alternative to the incremental-counter design because each remaining call would still be O(N), and reducing call frequency changes per-operation validation granularity (a later op in a batch is currently validated against state reflecting earlier ops in the same batch), which would need its own separate safety review; it is lateral on cost and weaker on safety than the chosen incremental-counter approach.

topic: A wrapper type for "life captured at admission" (which
canonical_claim: A wrapper type for "life captured at admission" (which would make the finalize-lambda life-capture type-checkable) was deliberately rejected as over-engineering for a single call site in the Stage-B catalog work; the delayed-writer-finalized test is the only guard against a silent regression there and must not be dropped or weakened.

topic: cas/ns/state/<life_id>/_ckpt stores {life_epoch, committed_through | none,...
canonical_claim: `cas/ns/state/<life_id>/_ckpt` stores `{life_epoch, committed_through | none, checkpoint_snapshot_id | none, last_epoch_seal | none}`; `committed_through` is the greatest transaction in durable acknowledged history, not the greatest key observed by a writer or LIST.

topic: The ref-snapshot/log Phase 2 optimization candidates include indexed or
canonical_claim: The ref-snapshot/log Phase 2 optimization candidates include indexed or chunked snapshots, lazy snapshot blocks, a bounded row cache, a per-round ref index, decoded-body reuse, and chunked namespace removal.

topic: The dominant remaining hot-pool byte cost is rewriting the
canonical_claim: The dominant remaining hot-pool byte cost is rewriting the full snapshot run in O(edges) per pass; the proposed remedy is O(delta)-write log-structured runs with periodic compaction.

topic: Catalog lifecycle needs durable reconciliation for interrupted Creating, Live
canonical_claim: Catalog lifecycle needs durable reconciliation for interrupted Creating, Live, and Removing transitions, including an actor that idempotently completes each transition.

topic: The strict ref-key grammar must parse <ns>/<incarnation>/{_log,_snap,_ckpt} canonically from
canonical_claim: The strict ref-key grammar must parse <ns>/<incarnation>/{_log,_snap,_ckpt} canonically from right to left and explicitly refuse legacy keys.

topic: S13 occurs when a hard-killed server leaves a same-UUID
canonical_claim: S13 occurs when a hard-killed server leaves a same-UUID mount body with the old `writer_epoch` and a future `expires_at_ms`; startup has already bumped the epoch, so the one-shot `claimMount` reports `LiveDoubleStart` and aborts before lease expiry.

topic: A CAS container recreated without persistent /var/lib/clickhouse gets a
canonical_claim: A CAS container recreated without persistent `/var/lib/clickhouse` gets a new `ServerUUID`, and the pool correctly refuses the foreign root claim with `CORRUPTED_DATA`; the refusal reports both UUIDs and three recovery paths.

topic: Rapid repeated crash-restart in S13 could wedge mount-lease self-adoption
canonical_claim: Rapid repeated crash-restart in S13 could wedge mount-lease self-adoption with `key '...ca_soak_ch1/mount' was touched while adopting our own mount slot`; the node stayed down with exit code 49 until the mount object was manually deleted. The original P1 availability bug was a cold-open adoption race in which GC fencing landed between the non-atomic GET and PUT in `Store::open`, causing exit 49 with `touched while adopting our own mount slot`. The cold-open path has no retry around the GET→PUT adoption window, so a fence landing there throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` `touched while adopting our own mount slot` during metadata load and leaves the container down with exit 49. A CA mount could wedge after rapid crash-restart because a GC leader legitimately fenced an expired lease while the renewal thread was blocked by synchronous `refreshViewForBeat` S3 reads, and the non-atomic self-adopt GET-to-CAS window had no retry.

topic: MountLeaseKeeper renewal can block beyond the 30-second TTL because
canonical_claim: `MountLeaseKeeper` renewal can block beyond the 30-second TTL because `prepareRenew` runs `Store::refreshViewForBeat`, which may wait for exclusive `view_gate` access and perform retired-view S3 reads. The old renewal path could let a slow retired-view refresh or `view_gate` drain delay the lease PUT beyond the 30-second TTL during RustFS retry storms, causing GC to fence a fully alive server; the observed RustFS read-error rate was about 19%.

topic: P1 was a chronic mount-lease race with about 26
canonical_claim: P1 was a chronic mount-lease race with about 26 occurrences on each node during the night; most self-healed by retry, but one S13 collision escalated to a permanent fail-closed exit 49.

topic: During Store teardown, a lease-renewal on_lost callback can re-arm
canonical_claim: During `Store` teardown, a lease-renewal `on_lost` callback can re-arm `remount_thread` after its only join because `scheduleRemount` does not guard shutdown, causing an unjoined `ThreadFromGlobalPoolImpl` to terminate the process. Store::~Store() can abort() the process: a lease-renewal failure during teardown re-arms remount_thread after the destructor's only join, because scheduleRemount() gates only on config.background_watermark and remount_running (never on a shutdown flag), so a fresh ThreadFromGlobalPool gets move-assigned into remount_thread after the join already passed; both ThreadFromGlobalPoolImpl::operator=(&&) and its destructor call abort() on a still-initialized target, so member destruction aborts. This is a guaranteed process crash under a realistic interleaving (an ordinary fenced-out or transiently-failing mount lease during DROP/disk-detach/server-shutdown), and was rated a blocker (risk 90) in the umbrella review of cas-gc-rebuild.

topic: The four B3 health columns are currently stamped identically
canonical_claim: The four B3 health columns are currently stamped identically on rows for mounts belonging to other servers in `StorageSystemContentAddressedMounts.cpp:159-162`; the rows remain truthful only because the documentation says the columns describe THIS server's health.

topic: A zombie replica returning during decommission cannot continue writing
canonical_claim: A zombie replica returning during decommission cannot continue writing because its renewal fails after the claim bumps the epoch; a full reopen sees the decommissioner's live lease and fails with `LiveDoubleStart`.

topic: A sustained object-store fault can fail the mount-lease renewal
canonical_claim: A sustained object-store fault can fail the mount-lease renewal PUT, let the lease deadline expire, trip the write fence, and cause every subsequent write to reject at `stageManifest` before attempting a write until self-remount recovers.; The S3-fault reproduction showed a mount-lease renewal PUT failing with `Code 499`, the write fence becoming lost pool-wide, self-remount being blocked for the fault duration, and recovery succeeding about 16 seconds after disarm without data loss or orphans.

topic: SingleWriterSlot::backgroundLoop treats any exception from renewOnce as terminal, while
canonical_claim: `SingleWriterSlot::backgroundLoop` treats any exception from `renewOnce` as terminal, while `renewOnce` can throw from `putOverwrite` before checking the returned token; a transient network fault is therefore misread as foreign-token supersession and burns the writer incarnation. The CI reproducer for the mount-lease self-race is a `putOverwrite` that applies to backend state and then throws a transient exception, followed by a confirmed mismatch against the stale token; the background loop must fence and invoke `on_lost` without process death. `SingleWriterSlot::backgroundLoop` continues after transient renewal failures while the confirmed lease deadline remains safe, but a definite `PreconditionFailed` mismatch always stops the loop and routes to `onRenewFailed` and self-remount recovery.; The root mechanism behind the #37 over-fencing defect is that `MountLeaseKeeper::renewOnce` (`CasServerRoot.cpp:913-931`) issues a single-shot direct `putOverwrite` (not routed through the 90-second write controller) and its `backgroundLoop` stops renewing forever on the FIRST transient exception, because the throw at `:926` fires before the foreign-token mismatch check at `:927-928`, conflating a brief network blip with genuine lease supersession.; Fix #37 distinguishes a confirmed token mismatch from a transient renewal exception: a completed PUT returning a foreign owner or epoch fences immediately, while a thrown `putOverwrite` is retried while the confirmed lease remains outside its safety margin.; The fail-close boundary for renewal is the lease deadline, with `now + lease_safety_margin >= lease_deadline` causing a fence when no successful renewal has refreshed the deadline; a proven supersession still fences immediately. The #37 lease-fencing contract is to retry transient renew failures while the last confirmed lease deadline remains valid and fence only after a confirmed deadline violation; `mount_fence.deadline_boot_ms` is refreshed only by genuine renew success.

topic: Review finding №9 is real: decommission can delete a
canonical_claim: Review finding №9 is real: decommission can delete a successor's fresh mount and epoch objects after releasing the impersonated lease, violating durable epoch monotonicity. Decommissioning can delete a successor mount's control objects because it releases the administrative claim before rereading and deleting current epoch, owner, and mount objects. Decommission must inspect every `DeleteOutcome`, abort the tail on any non-`Deleted` result, and delete mount before the claimed epoch and owner so successor objects cannot be reclaimed. The decommission tail must delete the farewell mount token first, then the epoch token captured under the claim, and owner last; every non-`Deleted` result aborts the tail and retains the slot.; A five-hour CA validation round found an unresolved architecture-level race in CAS pool decommission/owner-retirement: after a mount's owner is deleted and its epoch is already gone, a same-UUID successor can recreate the mount untouched by the owner check, and decommission's delete then removes the live successor's owner anchor; a symmetric owner-token check alone cannot close this because the owner's token never changes on resume, so a fix needs either a symmetric successor-side recheck or a condemn-marker two-phase retirement touching the claim/resume protocol, not just `CasDecommission.cpp`.; The decommission owner-anchor tombstone race remains deferred: a same-UUID successor can be recreated between the liveness recheck and owner CAS, and the operational rule is not to run `DROP POOL MEMBER` while the victim may be restarting.

topic: Review finding №11 is a narrow metadata leak: a
canonical_claim: Review finding №11 is a narrow metadata leak: a build allocated before registration can outlive namespace drop and GC reclamation, then create a reborn Live-but-ownerless empty ref table.

topic: SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED DROP POOL MEMBER bypasses the read_only
canonical_claim: `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED DROP POOL MEMBER` bypasses the `read_only` check used by other mutating CAS entry points, allowing an observe-only disk to decommission a peer.

topic: Pool::openForDecommission must force background_watermark = true; otherwise a read-only
canonical_claim: `Pool::openForDecommission` must force `background_watermark = true`; otherwise a read-only host disk does not renew the roughly 30-second administrative lease and a long drain can abort without cleanup or a report.

topic: A mount renewal against a vanished backing-store slot must
canonical_claim: A mount renewal against a vanished backing-store slot must throw `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`, not `LOGICAL_ERROR`, because constructing the latter aborts debug and ASan builds.; A mount-lease renewal mismatch under the keeper's own `(uuid, epoch)` can construct `LOGICAL_ERROR` and abort ASan or debug builds; the intended response is fail-closed uncertainty with a fence and self-remount. For a same-uuid, same-epoch, unfenced mount body, `MountLeaseKeeper::onRenewMismatch` throws `ABORTED` with state-uncertainty diagnostics and relies on fencing plus self-remount rather than constructing `LOGICAL_ERROR`. For a same-uuid body with a different writer epoch, `onRenewMismatch` throws `ABORTED` as the normal superseded fencing outcome and reports `superseded by a newer incarnation`. The former `MountLeaseKeeper::onRenewMismatch` classifier handled GC-fenced same-uuid bodies, different-uuid bodies, and vanished bodies but had no branch for same-uuid, same-epoch, unfenced bodies. An earlier renewal PUT can land while its client-side timeout loses the acknowledgement, bumping the mount token or sequence; the next retry then presents a stale token and reaches the classifier gap even though the body looks self-owned. Phase A classifies same-uuid/same-epoch/unfenced as `same_epoch_state_uncertain` with `ABORTED`, same-uuid/different-epoch as `superseded` with `ABORTED`, foreign uuid as `LOGICAL_ERROR`, and absent body as `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`.; Renewal mismatches are classified by the current mount body: an own fenced body is reported as `fenced_by_gc`, a newer own epoch as superseded, a foreign UUID as a foreign writer, and an unexplained mismatch remains a loud fail-closed exception.; After `PreconditionFailed` in renewal or adoption, the mount-lease code re-reads the slot body and classifies the refusal by body contents rather than by token alone.

topic: mountWritable previously armed bootMsNow() + TTL after an unbounded
canonical_claim: `mountWritable` previously armed `bootMsNow() + TTL` after an unbounded `materialization_grace_ms`; if the grace consumed the TTL, a successor could reclaim the slot while the predecessor armed an already-superseded claim.

topic: A diagnostic process opening a live CA pool through
canonical_claim: A diagnostic process opening a live CA pool through `Pool::mountWritable` can fail ownership claiming because the running server legitimately owns the server root; the failure is indistinguishable from a real mount-ownership defect unless the tool's contract is made explicit.

topic: Forcing only the owner anchor cannot mount a foreign
canonical_claim: Forcing only the owner anchor cannot mount a foreign pool because the mount slot retains the predecessor's `server_uuid` and ordinary `claimMount` rejects it as `ForeignOwner`; a graceful shutdown leaves that slot with `min_active == UINT64_MAX` rather than deleting it.

topic: cleanupOrphanedBirthCkptBestEffort can delete a successor writer's current _ckpt because
canonical_claim: `cleanupOrphanedBirthCkptBestEffort` can delete a successor writer's current `_ckpt` because it resolves the checkpoint key and token at cleanup time without proving ownership by the rejected creation attempt.; Rejected-birth checkpoint cleanup must be bound to the exact object version created by the attempt and to a catalog state or fence proving exclusive ownership; otherwise the cleanup must retain responsibility.

topic: Manual GC, rebuild, and system-table access can race metadata
canonical_claim: Manual GC, rebuild, and system-table access can race metadata shutdown because scheduler pointers and `cas_store` are used after mutex unlock and lazy creation can resurrect the scheduler after shutdown.
